| | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 | TTM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Qtr | Dec24 | Mar25 | Jun25 | Sep25 | Dec25 | Mar26 | Jun26 | Sep26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 158 | 156 | 176 | 176 | 205 | 214 | 267 | 355 |
| OPM | 6% | 5% | 4.4% | 4.1% | 5% | 9% | 17% | 15% |
| PAT | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 4 | 11 | 31 | 38 |

**Shareholding**
- Promoter steady at 66.35%.
- FII went from 0.02% to 0.87% in Sep-26. That is one quarter, not a trend.

**Named cause**
- Optical fibre prices spiked on AI/data-centre demand (forum and industry reports cite about 3x in 18 months) and Q2 revenue doubled YoY.
- The 10-year OPM history shows the same spike in FY19 (16%) during the last fibre boom, followed by a bust to 8%.
- This is a cyclical price spike, not a structural shift.

**Other flags**
- FY26 CFO was ₹-21 cr.
- Debtor days are about 96 and the cash conversion cycle is 124 days.
- The stock is up about 153% YTD.
- Sector peers fell 31% after the October 2026 AI-stock rout.

**Bull case**
- If the H1 run-rate holds, PAT would be about ₹140 cr. At 10x, market cap would be ₹1,400 cr, 1.5x.

**Kill criteria**
- OPM below 10%.
- Fibre spot prices roll over.
- CFO stays negative in H1 FY27.

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:ICICIGI:q3fy27-combined-ratio-103-5-or-better`
- **Method:** management-tone-vs-delivery · **P(ours)** 0.55 · **P(base)** 0.40 · resolve by 2027-02-15
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (Oct-2026): combined ratio 104.5% (102.7% ex-CAT losses of ₹118 cr) vs 103.9% in Q2 FY26; H1 FY27 105.2% (104.2% ex-CAT) vs 103.0% — H1 included provisions on motor third-party reserves after a Supreme Court judgement; management: 'we do not anticipate any need for any further requirement of provision' on that; industry motor combined ratio deteriorating (industry CoR 116.8% in Q1 FY27); GDPI +5.4% H1 vs industry +8.9%, fire de-growth easing. Q3 FY26 transcript (19-Jan-2026): Q3 FY26 combined ratio 103.1% (n basis); 9M FY26 103.1%. Q2 FY27 PAT ₹1,031 cr (+27.5%).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Management sounds confident the TP reserve hit was one-off and Q3 is usually light on catastrophe losses; Q2 ex-CAT was already 102.7%. The delivery record on 'no further provisions' statements in Indian GI is mixed, but here the arithmetic supports it. We go above the backward-looking base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Naive: average of the last three reported quarterly combined ratios (Q3 FY26 103.1%, Q1 FY27 ~105.9% implied from H1, Q2 FY27 104.5%) is ~104.5%; chance of printing ≤103.5% is ~40%.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if ICICI Lombard's reported combined ratio (n basis, including CAT losses, as stated in the Q3 FY27 press release/presentation) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≤103.5%.
- **Resolution source:** ICICI Lombard Q3 FY27 press release / investor presentation (NSE)
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/ICICIGI_19102026131424_SE_Intimation_Earnings_call_transcript.pdf; https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/ICICIGI_19012026180922_SE_Intimation_-_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf; https://www.screener.in/company/ICICIGI/
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified

| **TTM Sep-26** | **2,406** | **11.8** | 246 | 208 adj | 137.6 adj | 185 | — | — | 12.9 |
*Equity + borrowings − cash − investments. NOPAT = core EBIT × (1 − tax). FY-end P/E = Yahoo close ÷ reported EPS.

**Re-derivations and adjustments.**
- **Other income** FY26 ₹32.2 cr `[AR26 n.22]` = deposits interest 19.5 + other interest 2.2 + MF gains/FV 7.5 + PPE gains 1.4 + misc 1.6 → 15% of PBT;
  core PBT = ₹188 cr. Screener nets the FY26 labour-code exceptional (₹11.99 cr) into Q3 "other income" (−3).
- **The FY26 revenue gross-up (good-but-misleading).** Materials (RM + inventory change) fell from **71.0%** of revenue (FY25) to **67.5%** (FY26) while
  other expenses rose from 11.7% to 14.3% (technical fee 1.07 → 97.5 cr). If physical material cost per unit was unchanged, revenue per unit rose
  ~5% (71.0/67.5 = 1.052) purely from selling at OEM prices instead of MHVSIL's transfer price `[EST]`. So FY26 "+4.8%" ≈ **flat like-for-like**,
  while M&HCV industry volume grew ~16% to ~480k `[T-Q4FY26; single-source, management]`. H1 FY26 was −3.6% reported (≈ −8% like-for-like), H2 FY26
  +12% reported (≈ +7%).
- **Revenue per industry vehicle** (₹ revenue ÷ M&HCV units): FY19 ₹40.7k; FY26 ₹45.4k reported, ~₹43.2k like-for-like (+6% in 7 years, ~0.9%/yr,
  below steel/price inflation) `[EST; industry volumes management-sourced]`. The "tonnage shift raises our content" story is not yet visible in the
  numbers.
- **Cash conversion.** CFO/EBITDA 41–129% (FY23–26); FY25 receivables ₹438 cr included ₹387 cr from MHVSIL, which unwound to ₹1 cr in FY26.
  H1 FY27 CFO ₹86 cr after an inventory build of ₹48 cr for the pre-buy `[Q2FY27 CF]`.
- **Customer concentration** `[AR26 n.32]`: Customer A ₹1,440 cr (66%), Customer B ₹214 cr (10%), MHVSIL ₹28 cr (FY26); in FY25 MHVSIL was 80%.

**The free-bed arithmetic (what the dispute is worth).** One-third of ~700 beds = ~233 beds. At ₹2.55 cr revenue per occupied bed, enforcing a full
one-third free IPD quota *on top of* today's ~7–9% would remove ~25% of paying IPD capacity: **~₹350 cr revenue** and, at a ~50% contribution margin
(doctor fees, consumables and part of staff are variable), **~₹170 cr of EBITDA (~60%)** `[EST]`. IMCL's own ask (10% IPD incl. medicines) would cost
roughly 10% of IPD consumables (~₹25 cr) plus forgone medicine charges on referred patients — **~₹25–50 cr EBITDA (10–18%)** `[EST]`. A market lease
rent for the site is unknown `[open item]`.
**Payback on new capacity:** not applicable — no expansion capex (CWIP ₹2.8 cr; capex ₹30–60 cr/yr is equipment replacement and upgrades).

body:
1. **No change.** The split by flag type fails on its own pre-registered terms: in the larger event sample pledge-only
   firms do not have fewer winners (WIN3 1.27×, same as ICR-only), and the tail signal of each single flag is
   regime-dependent. Weak interest cover alone keeps the starter cap (its tail is real, 1.7× halving / 2.9× failure,
   and was the main single-flag signal in 2022–25).
2. **Post-hoc observation (not adopted, needs its own test):** grading by *number* of flags looks more stable than
   grading by *type*. "Both" (pledge > 25% **and** ICR < 1.5x, ~4.7% of events) halves 30% of the time in 12 months
   (4.2×), fails within 3 years 26% (9.4×), in both E periods (H12 3.5× / 3.7×), and in P fails 57% (4.4×) with
   −45 pp 3-year excess. But in E it still triples 23.5% of the time (1.5×), so a 0-new-money rule would still cost
   winners there. A future pre-registered test on fresh events (2026+ results) could ask whether "both flags → 0 new
   money" holds out of sample. Until then: when both fire, the balance-sheet question should be answered *before*
   even the starter position (judgement, not a code rule).
3. Pledge > 50% is the strongest single tail marker (H12 4.0×, FAIL3 9.2× in E; failure 3.4× and −42 pp excess in P)
   but also carries more winners in E (1.57×) — high variance again, not a clean negative.
